brand_voice_note: Warm, sensory, and quietly luxurious - it treats a hand sanitizer like a fine fragrance and a small daily ritual worth savoring.

concepts.primary_text:
Your hand sanitizer should not smell like a hospital.

Elysium wraps your hands in creamy vanilla, blooming peony, and glowing amber woods. It looks and smells like a modern perfume, then leaves your hands feeling incredibly soft and beautifully scented.

Kills 99.9% of the most common germs. Infused with skincare so nothing feels tight or sticky.
concepts.headline: Sanitizer that smells like perfume
concepts.why_it_works: Elysium's rich vanilla-amber scent is its most desirable feature, so leading with the sensory payoff sells the everyday-luxury feeling instantly.
concepts.visual_direction: The frosted Elysium bottle standing on a linen runner at a softly lit vanity, with a single dried peony stem in a small vase beside it.

concepts.primary_text:
Tired of sanitizer that leaves your hands dry, sticky, and smelling of harsh chemicals?

Caela is a fine mist that's never heavy or sticky - bright citrus, soft white florals, and a whisper of green tea. Formulated with 65% v/v ethyl alcohol to kill 99.9% of the most common germs, then infused with skincare that leaves your hands soft and hydrated.

And it twists open with one hand. One spray, done.
concepts.headline: Clean hands, no sticky residue
concepts.why_it_works: Every sanitizer user knows the dry, sticky, chemical-smell friction, so naming it and answering it directly makes Caela's soft, fresh formula the obvious fix.
concepts.visual_direction: The frosted sage-green Caela bottle on a bright marble kitchen counter with a fresh lemon wedge and loose green tea leaves alongside.

concepts.primary_text:
"It's just a sanitizer." Not this one.

Amara pairs cool lavender, rosy geranium, and soft white musk with a patent-pending capless one-handed twist design - 650 sprays that twist open with one hand, no fumbling for a lid.

Vegan and cruelty-free, free from phthalates and sulfates, and made in the USA. At $12, it earns its spot on your counter.
concepts.headline: The 650-spray twist design
concepts.why_it_works: The biggest hesitation at $12 is 'why pay more than drugstore sanitizer,' so leading with the patented one-handed design and 650-spray value answers the objection head on.
concepts.visual_direction: The frosted lilac Amara bottle standing on a matte charcoal desk beside folded reading glasses and a ceramic tray under clean studio light.
